rejected.title: Christian sexual ethics
card: Christian sexual ethics is the teaching on how sexuality should be understood and lived. It covers topics such as marriage, sex outside marriage, celibacy and same-sex relationships.
Scripture
The Bible is a main source. Christians read passages on marriage and sexual conduct, and they may interpret them differently for life today.
Tradition
Church teaching handed down over time also shapes belief. It includes the work of theologians, church councils and official statements. Some churches give tradition more weight than others.

Churches differ on questions such as same-sex relationships. Some teach that marriage is only between a man and a woman. Others bless or marry same-sex couples. Differences often come from how a church reads scripture and weighs tradition.
rejected.remember: Christian sexual ethics draws on scripture and tradition, and how a church reads them can lead to different views.

a.q: Why may two Christian churches teach different things about same-sex relationships?
opts: They read scripture and weigh tradition differently
One church accepts the Bible and the other rejects it
One church uses tradition and the other uses no source
They disagree on whether Jesus was a historical person
a.why: Churches draw on the same kinds of sources but may interpret scripture differently and give tradition different weight. The option about rejecting the Bible is tempting, but churches on both sides of the question treat the Bible as an authority.
a.clue: Think about how the sources are read, not whether they are used.

b.q: A minister in Newcastle says, "Our teaching on marriage comes from how our church has understood the Bible over many centuries." Which source is the minister mainly pointing to?
opts: Tradition, which has shaped how scripture is read
Scripture alone, read with no church teaching
Personal opinion, which each member decides
Public opinion, which changes with each decade
b.why: Centuries of church understanding is tradition, and the minister links it to how the Bible is read. The tempting option is scripture alone, but the minister is describing the church's long reading of it, not the text on its own.
b.clue: The minister speaks of what the church has understood over time.

draft.title: Christian sexual ethics
card: Christian sexual ethics is teaching on how to understand and live out sexuality. It covers topics such as marriage, celibacy and same-sex relationships.
Scripture
the Bible, which Christians read for teaching on marriage and sexual conduct. Christians may interpret the same passages in different ways.
Tradition
teaching handed down in the church over time, such as statements by church councils and theologians. Churches may give it different weight.

Churches differ on questions such as same-sex relationships. Some teach that marriage is between a man and a woman, while others bless or marry same-sex couples. These differences can come from how a church reads scripture and weighs tradition.
draft.remember: Scripture and tradition guide Christian teaching on sexuality, and churches can read and weigh them differently.

a.q: Two churches in Perth both treat the Bible as an authority, yet they teach different things about same-sex marriage. What best explains this?
opts: They interpret passages and weigh tradition differently
One has rejected the Bible as a source of teaching
One follows tradition and has dropped all scripture
Christian teaching has no sources on sexuality
a.why: Churches can share the Bible as an authority and still reach different views, because they may interpret passages differently and give tradition different weight. The option about rejecting the Bible is tempting, but the question says both churches treat the Bible as an authority.
a.clue: Both churches use the Bible, so look at how they use it.

b.q: Which of these is an example of tradition, rather than scripture, shaping Christian teaching on marriage?
opts: A church council's statement on marriage made long ago
A verse about marriage read aloud at a wedding
A member's own view on how couples should live
A news poll on what Australians think of marriage
b.why: A council's statement is teaching handed down in the church over time, which is tradition. The verse read at a wedding is scripture, so it is the most tempting wrong option. A personal view and a news poll are not church teaching handed down over time.
b.clue: Tradition is church teaching handed down over time.

a.best: They interpret passages and weigh tradition differently

b.best: A church council's statement on marriage made long ago

'Christian teaching has no sources on sexuality' is plainly absurd. A Year 12 student can pick the answer by elimination without knowing the idea.

a.q: Two churches in Perth both treat the Bible as an authority, yet they teach different things about same-sex marriage. What best explains this?
